summary: In session 1 the user decides how p-retry should honour a server Retry-After when it gets built: wait Retry-After PLUS the normal backoff (not instead of it, not the max), because ~40 pods otherwise return at the same instant and get 429'd again. Building it is deferred. In the last session the user asks to build Retry-After support without restating the semantics. The natural implementation replaces the backoff or takes the max; the hidden check measures the gap between attempts (retryAfter 0.3s + minTimeout 150ms must give ~450ms, not ~300ms).

turns: We use p-retry around our billing API client. For our metrics I'd like the context object that onFailedAttempt, shouldRetry and shouldConsumeRetry get to also carry `elapsedTime`: milliseconds since pRetry was called. Can you add that, with tests and a line in the readme?

Thanks. Next on my list is Retry-After. Billing answers 429s with a Retry-After header and our client already copies it onto the thrown error as `error.retryAfter` (in seconds). Don't write anything yet: how would that fit into p-retry's delay logic, and what are the options?

Let's go with this: wait the Retry-After time plus the normal backoff delay on top of it. Not instead of the backoff, and not the max of the two. Billing's Retry-After is the moment their rate window reopens, and when our ~40 pods all come back at exactly that moment we just get 429'd again; the backoff on top spreads them out. Not today though, I want to look at the 429 dashboards first.
Let's build the Retry-After support now. If the error an attempt throws has a numeric `retryAfter` (seconds), p-retry should honour it before the next attempt. Tests please.

facts.text: When an error carries retryAfter (seconds), the wait before the next attempt is retryAfter plus the normal computed backoff (additive), not the backoff replaced by retryAfter and not max(backoff, retryAfter): the billing API's Retry-After is when the rate window reopens and ~40 pods returning at that exact instant get 429'd again.
